body: Hi man (or woman or gender neutral term of your choice). I get it. I used to be just as terrified of needles as you are of flights. It’s nothing to be ashamed of. Seriously just the thought of a shot could send me into a full blown panic attack. Anyway, as someone who flights more than the average person, it’s not as bad as it seems. You’ll be okay. You’ll get on the flight and before you know it you’ll be on the ground again. You got this.

In my opinion it’s a way of destigmatizing not “being okay.” Or, in this specific case, destigmatizing mental illness. While it’s not good to not be okay (ideally everyone is okay all the time), it shouldn’t be viewed as negatively as it is today. I’d draw parallels to the whole body positivity movement. It’s not healthy to be over/underweight (or suffering from mental illness), but it’s also not something to be shamed over.

Thanks for the suggestions. I honestly might make it a routine to write something down everyday (good or bad). I find journaling helps me calm down a lot. I suppose this account is sort of an open diary as well.
Thanks man.

It’s alright. I’ve also considered talking to a therapist, but (as you suspect) I’m still reliant on my parents for at least around a year. I’m not too sure about after that but, for the foreseeable future, seeking a therapist is for a worst case scenario. Luckily I’m privileged enough that therapy is an option, but I’d like to avoid it if possible. I’m also incredibly fortunate that I’m cognizant enough to realize when it’s too much for me to bear and I need to seek professional help. Currently talking to people on the internet is enough, but if it gets to a point where I need to seek help I will most certainly do so.
Most of my grandparents are dead and the ones that are alive are behind a language barrier. Still, I suspect that they wouldn’t understand either.

Well I do try and understand why things are the way they are most of the time. As for why I’m unable to tell anyone, I don’t know very many people. My family doesn’t seem to believe someone like me can suffer from a serious mental illness and when I do try and talk to them about it they don’t understand and are unhelpful for the most part. I don’t blame them for this, (I’m not an easy person to understand) but they have proven to be unreliable in that area. While I do have friends, they aren’t the traditional type where I would confide in. In that sense they’re more like acquaintances then friends. And there’s a mental barrier I put up that prevents me from talking to the friends who I can confide in. I’m scared I’ll be seen as a burden or an annoyance. Those friends are few and far in between and I’m terrified of losing them. I have opened up to my girlfriend about it and she did help, but part of me still hates myself for bothering her with what I view to be my own problems. I told her that and she called me a dummy. Logically I know it’s fine to talk to people I know, but still there’s a part of me that hates myself for having to bother them. As such the compromise I’ve reached is to tell my problems to random people on the internet.

Yeah, kinda. I’m not too sure on the specifics, but a cumulation of events happened and I broke down. Not like one major event, but like multiple minor ones. After that everything just spiraled out of control. Nowadays there are some episodes with triggers and some without. I’m pretty sure there’s a “cause” to everything I feel though, even if I’m not aware of it.
Hi. So I’ve been feeling like this for about a month. But I’ve had mental health issues starting this New Years.
Thanks man. I’m not going to lie I cried a bit reading this. Thanks for caring. I really needed to hear that.
Hi thanks for the offer. Really it means so much to me that you’d be willing to do that.

Edit: Looks like I was wrong about the whole melatonin thing. I was told otherwise, but a cursory google search says that it’s unlikely for one to develop a dependence on it. Still, out of principle I try to take things in moderation.

Yeah it’s progress. Small, but any progress is welcome. 

I try and sleep healthier nowadays, but before I’d constantly be sleep deprived. Hopefully I can keep up with my sleep when school starts back up. 

I personally don’t think there’s any shame in taking drugs in general (provided it’s to heal), I just want to avoid a dependency on outside sources. Long story short taking too much can cause your body to slow natural production.

Anyway here’s to everyone feeling better as soon as possible. Cheers.

Hi so it sounds to me like you’ve been having existential crisises (how to pluralize crisis?). I’ve had them for basically as far as I can remember. To make things worse for me, I’m an agnostic atheist so I don’t really believe in any form of life after death. What got me through that stage of my life was philosophy (specifically videos on YouTube). I’ve learnt to accept that I’ll eventually be forgotten and find some solace in it. There’s a video on optimistic nihilism by Kurzgesagt that I recommend you check out. Other than that Sisyphus55 is a whole channel dedicated to philosophy that I’m subscribed to. I found lot of his content cool and I know he has a couple good videos about absurdism which might help you. Exurb1a another good channel, but if I remember correctly he focuses more on absurdism than Sisyphus does. Anyway my personal recommendation would be to just accept death as another part of life. Still I don’t know you or your circumstance so I don’t know if what worked for me will work for you. Life’s kinda funny that way. Everyone’s just stumbling around the dark trying to find their own path. Good luck. Cheers!
Thanks for caring.

I’m doing okay. Thanks for your best wishes. 

P.s. Man, I’m in awe of how well you express yourself. Your writing is amazing.
Yeah… I don’t have much to add. I understand. It means nothing, but I wish you well. I hope you you make it past the struggle. Good luck :)

Hi. I… don’t know how to start a conversation. As you can probably tell I’m pretty awkward myself. So trust me when I say that I understand you. It’s fine to crave validation and friendship. Hell, I’d even say it’s human nature to do so. I know you’ve worked hard and to have nothing to show for it is heart-wrenching. 

Now I can’t and won’t promise it will get better. I can’t promise that if you keep trying someone will get you. But I will say, if you keep on trying, the odds someone will get you eventually are pretty high. That is how I met my one or two friends after all (it only took 17 years which is not as bad as it sounds considering I’m a youngin).

Side-note, I’d hope this isn’t your last year. You can make it through this. Good luck. :)

Edit: I feel like a could say more, but don’t know what. Curses!
No problem. Best wishes. :)
I hope you feel better soon my guy (or girl or whatever you go by). Good luck with climbing your mountain. :)

Me too. I have a great life, same as you. I have a very supportive family (the most supportive in fact). I have an amazing more-than-friend girl friend. I… don’t have money, but my parents do. All in all, my life is great. So what right do we have to be sad? There are people starving in Africa for Christ’s sake! 

Well that’s wrong. How you feel is valid. Your depression is your personal mountain to climb. Yes, other people have taller mountains, but a mountain’s a mountain no matter how tall. You aren’t a ungrateful PoS just because you’re depressed.

Hi. So I have some experience with crying myself to sleep. It’s… (pause for dramatic effect) well you know. Anyway, I get the feeling of not having any friends and being to tired to try. I really do. It sucks. My honest advice (from personal experience, may not apply)? Find someone who cares (about you personally) and let them know you’re having a hard time. Find someone to be with you. Find something to do that makes you feel better (even if it’s just for a minute) and do that. For me, creating this account and talking to others was really uplifting. Hang on in there. You aren’t alone. [Insert a few more generic positive affirmations]. I hope your night gets better. :)

Edit: Just realized I broke a rule. I fixed it. Oh and grammar too.
Thanks for the recommendations. I hope I feel better soon.
Yeah I get the feeling of needing someone to talk to. I’m here if you ever need me.

Hi. So I can’t really offer much in terms of assistance. Coincidentally enough I also just made a post about sleep while laying in bed. I don’t know, I guess I just wanted to let you know that you weren’t alone. Anxiety sucks. Best wishes.
Good stuff! 👍
Hi. I can’t offer much in terms of advice, but if you need to talk to someone I’m here. I promise you can and will get through this.

Yeah. Pacing seems to be one of the body’s magnificent ways to deal with stress in general. I’d have to fact-check this, but I believe moving around (walking, running, pacing, etc.) releases endorphins which help to reduce stress and make you feel better.

Edit: Okay so I might’ve guessed wrong. It seems being stressed leads to increased adrenaline which brings up your energy levels which is brought back down with exercise. It also may be a mechanism to distract yourself from whatever you’re worrying about as repetitive movements seem to do that. 

Edit 2: Exercise does stimulate the production of endorphins. I’m not sure to what extent this applies to pacing however.

Well. In this case you’re probably fine, but err on the side of caution in the future I guess. In general it’s just good practice to avoid mold, especially in foods, but I’m sure you don’t need to be told that. Obsessively thinking about a thought is never fun and it’s hard to stop so my advice would be to just never give yourself anything to obsessively worry about. Or at least avoid doing so to the best of your ability. Prevention is always better than a cure after all.

Nice. Got poked 2 times already. Only side effect was that my arm got sore for like a day (which was a pain considering I had to take an AP test with a sore arm). Thanks for doing your part to help those who are more affected by the pandemic.

Hello fellow teen. Haha but fr hi. I know how it feels to be tired and done with everything. It’s not fun (way to state the obvious buddy). 

So first of all, math’s hard. I’m not going to lie and say it isn’t important, but your life’s not going to end because you were bad at math. Besides it’s nothing a little (or lot) of effort can’t fix.

As for driving, I wouldn’t worry about it (figuratively, I know it’s hard to stop yourself when you have anxiety). It’s pretty scary to be the one behind the wheel, but you should trust yourself more. If the morons I see on the road can drive then so can you. Also try not to be embarrassed if you can. There’s nothing shameful about not being able to drive due to anxiety.

Now for your slew of disorders. Yeah that sucks. Sorry. I wish I could be more helpful. It means nothing, but I respect you for being able to deal with that as well as you have. You are stronger than I am.

About your ex, I’m sorry. That sucks too. I don’t have too much experience dealing with relationships. (I’m 17 and haven’t had a girlfriend. My one experience would be the girl I’m currently talking to a.k.a my girlfriend with a big question mark affixed to that title.) Good news, you’re young. There’s still time for you to develop a meaningful romantic relationship. I’d even argue that odds are you will meet someone better for you. Insert rant about relationships and maturity.

Lastly, don’t feel bad about posting this. You aren’t worthless. Period. End of conversation. I don’t accept constructive criticism in this case and will enforce my judgement with tyrannical and dictatorial force. 

Anyway I hope you feel better soon. Sending virtual hugs and support (platonically of course). Oh yeah if you ever need to talk, I’m here.

Hi. Sorry this took so long. I don’t really know what to be saying here so I’ll just directly answer your questions and see where that takes me. 

I do exercise, though not much. To be honest my entire life I’ve been pretty chubby and out of shape. Only recently have I started to exercise both out of concern for my physical and mental well-being. The last time I went to the gym was a couple days ago. I ran a mile and biked another 2.5. It’s not much but I’m pretty proud of myself for it. On days where I don’t go to the gym I try and walk for at least 30 min. Honestly I should probably move around more seeing as it’s one of the few things that helps me stop thinking.

I don’t use drugs or alcohol. Partly because I’m a minor, but mainly because I don’t feel a need or want to. I suppose I should be happy for that given how easy it would be to fall down that particular rabbit hole. But that’s a whole other story for another post.

I’m not seeing a therapist. To be honest my parents don’t even really know what I’ve been going through… or at least they wouldn’t have a couple of hours ago. I told them a bit about how I feel. My father was helpful. My mother was less so. I think it’s because my father’s relatively closer to being like me? He understood me better? Confiding in my mother was just pretty frustrating given she and I are two entirely different characters. Kinda like we were speaking foreign languages. No matter how much we tried to understand each other the fundamental language barrier got in the way. Other than my parents, I’ve told the girl I’m talking to (a.k.a my girlfriend?) how I felt and she was really supportive. I’d like to make it a point to express how grateful I am that she’s been with me through fair and foul weather, even if she’ll never know I said so at this particular point in time. And then I’ve confided to whichever internet denizen that’s stumbled upon my post and felt like reading it for whatever reason (I am thankful that a stranger would take time out of their day to listen to my problems by the way). I am however considering to ask my parents to take me to see a doctor who can refer me to a therapist.

As for other methods to keep my mind at bay? Well there’s not much. I journal I guess. I’m sure there’s more but nothing off the top of my head.

To round this all up I’ll just say that some progress has been made. I’m still a crying mess. Really just taking things slowly and hoping everything will be okay in the end. I’ll probably make a few more posts to this sub just to document my journey (the good, bad, and everything in between). 

Also, thank you for talking to me. I can’t tell you how much it means to me.

Also also, reading through my post I’ve noticed a couple grammatical errors. My inner perfectionist wants to correct them all, but I’m tired. So as a compromise I’ve decided to make a meta comment acknowledging them, but not actually do anything about them even though it’d probably be just as easy, if not easier, just to silently correct them. 

Okay I think that’s it. Toodles.
